newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Ethiopian premier visits pariah Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian premier visits pariah Nigeria.

text.p: Ethiopian Prime Minister Meles Zenawi arrived in the Nigerian capital Abuja on Monday on a two-day official visit, airport officials said.
They said he was welcomed at Abuja international airport by military ruler General Sani Abacha amidst traditional drumming.

Until recently visits by international statesmen to Nigeria have been rare since Africa's most populous nation hanged nine minority rights activists including author Ken Saro-Wiwa for murder last November.
Zenawi is the second prime minister this month to visit Nigeria, which is shunned by the West for alleged human rights abuses and lack of democracy.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan of Turkey was in Abuja three weeks ago and the two countries signed a broad range of economic agreements.
Ethiopian embassy officials in Lagos said Zenawi's visit was to promote both political and economic relations between the two African nations.
"We have a trade agreement which has expired and which will be renewed," one said. There were no figures immediately available on the volume of trade between the two nations.
Zenawi is being accompanied by Ethiopian businessmen including the general manager of Ethiopian Airlines, which flies to Lagos three times a week from Addis Ababa.

Like many other visitors to Nigeria in recent times, Zenawi will confine his stay to the north where he is scheduled to tour the wholly Nigerian-owned Nasco Industries, which manufactures biscuits and cereals in the highland city of Jos.
Zenawi has close ties to Washington with whom relations with Nigeria have deteriorated over the slow pace of democratisation and alleged human rights violations in the African nation.
Nigeria plunged into crisis in 1993 when the army annulled a vote to restore democracy.

Abacha seized power in the confusion that followed and is implementing a programme he says will restore democracy fully in 1998 but which critics say is a ruse and point to the detention of many people including the presumed winner of the annulled vote.
